answer: The strongest lever is simple: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because saffron only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, bridge is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
